responsibility: This module is GCC’s language-independent option-definition, generation, parsing, and compiler-side option-management subsystem. It centers on the declarative .opt catalogs such as common.opt and params.opt plus the AWK generators that read, normalize, validate, and turn those descriptions into the cl_options/cl_enums tables, option-state fields, include dependencies, and documentation-URL mappings used throughout the compiler. On top of that generated metadata, the opts and opts-common families provide the core runtime machinery for looking up and decoding switches, handling aliases, warnings, and propagated option strings, while opts-global integrates option processing with compiler-global state, front-end/common/target handlers, deferred post-parse actions, and help/diagnostic behavior. The module also covers user-facing option services such as misspelling suggestions and completion, diagnostic-output option handling, diagnostic naming and documentation links, debug-format and producer-string policy, GNU make jobserver cooperation, and the opt_problem support used to attach rich missed-optimization context to optimization failures, making this the shared infrastructure that defines what GCC command-line options exist and how they are interpreted, validated, surfaced, and propagated across compilation stages.
